summary: Phramonchai Saitanaporn works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Sydney, attested in 2009, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, and also studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.
Phrapongsak K. is a Buddhist studies scholar who in 2015 held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and an open-recruitment researcher at the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.

Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Radcliffe College and earning a PhD from Harvard (~1969–1973), she held professorships at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Yale University (emeritus 2004).
Pierre Arènes is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under André Bareau and held an attested post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique in 2003–2004.

Pierre Bourdieu was a French philosopher and scholar who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, Lycée Louis-Barthou, and the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lille University, EHESS, and Collège de France (1981–2001).
Pierre Chantraine was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes between ~1920 and ~1927. He held a post at the University of Paris from ~1938 to 1969.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry (1963–1967), the Chair of Sanskrit at EPHE (1967–2004), and positions at EHESS, the Société Asiatique, and the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Leiden University by 1991 and held a post there as a research fellow, attested in 1996.
Pieter Hendrik Pott was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He served as a curator at the Museum Volkenkunde (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

Pietro Merlo studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia in 1867. He taught at the University of Pavia from 1877, becoming an extraordinary professor in 1880 and full professor of comparative linguistics of ancient and Romance languages in 1885.

Piotr Balcerowicz is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Warsaw, BHU, the University of Hamburg (PhD 1999), and the Polish Academy of Sciences (habilitation 2005). He became Professor of Indology at Warsaw in 2011.

Piotr Klafkowski was a Tibetologist and linguist. He earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski, and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and later taught Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka was an Indonesian linguist, Indologist, and historian. He earned a doctorate at Leiden University (~1921–1926) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom, worked at Dinas Purbakala, and later served as professor at Gadjah Mada University, University of Indonesia, and Udayana University.

Polly Young-Eisendrath studied at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis, and undertook Zen training under Philip Kapleau. In 1994, she was appointed clinical associate professor in Psychiatry at the University of Vermont.

Popatbhai Ambashankar Mankad was active in Indology and history/archaeology. He held engineering posts as State Engineer at Junagadh, Chief Engineer for Jodhpur State, and Chief Officer and Engineer for Hyderabad Municipality.
Pori Park is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and held an appointment as assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Potprecha Cholvijarn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Chulalongkorn University and the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin, and served as a special lecturer at Chulalongkorn University, attested in 2011.
Poulami Ray works in history and archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and held a position as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.
